title: Inclusion-Exclusion: Applications to Number Theory and Combinatorics
description: Applies the inclusion-exclusion principle to connect combinatorics and number theory. Proves sieve formulas (2-set and 3-set), Euler's totient via IE sieve (φ(pq)=(p-1)(q-1)), surjection counting (|Surj(n,k)| = Σ (-1)^j C(k,j)(k-j)^n), derangement formula (D(n) = Σ (-1)^k C(n,k)(n-k)!), derangement recurrence, divisor-totient identity (Σ_{d|n} φ(d) = n), and alternating binomial sum. 41 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. Fully machine-verified using Mathlib's Nat.totient and Finset.card lemmas.
originalContributions: sieve_two / sieve_three: |U \ (A ∪ B)| and three-set inclusion-exclusion
totient_prime_product: φ(pq) = (p-1)(q-1) for distinct primes via IE sieve
derangement_count: D(n) = Σ_{k=0}^n (-1)^k C(n,k)(n-k)! = n! Σ (-1)^k/k!

overview.historicalContext: Inclusion-exclusion (Sylvester 1883, though the principle is older) counts elements in unions/intersections via alternating sums. It connects diverse counting problems: Euler's totient (count integers coprime to n), derangements (permutations with no fixed points), surjections, and Stirling numbers. The divisor-totient identity Σ_{d|n} φ(d) = n is a classical result connecting multiplicative functions.
overview.problemStatement: Apply inclusion-exclusion to prove: sieve formulas, Euler totient for prime products, surjection count, derangement formula and recurrence, and the divisor-totient identity.
overview.text: The IE principle: |A₁ ∪ ... ∪ Aₖ| = Σ|Aᵢ| - Σ|Aᵢ∩Aⱼ| + ... (alternating sums). Applied to 'bad' sets: |U \ (A₁ ∪ ... ∪ Aₖ)| = Σ_{S ⊆ [k]} (-1)^|S| |U ∩ ∩_{i∈S} Aᵢ|. For surjections: the 'bad' events are 'element j is not in the image'. For derangements: the 'bad' events are 'element i is a fixed point'. The divisor-totient identity follows from the multiplicativity of φ.
overview.proofStrategy: Prove the 2-set and 3-set sieve formulas using Finset.card_sdiff_add_card and card_union_add_card_inter. Use Nat.sum_totient for the divisor-totient identity. Prove derangement recurrence algebraically.
keyInsights: Sieve = complement of bad events: |good| = |total| - |bad|, corrected for overlaps
Totient via sieve: φ(n) = n · Π_{p|n}(1-1/p) for prime p
Derangement formula: D(n)/n! → 1/e as n→∞ (alternating exponential series)
Divisor-totient identity: Σ_{d|n} φ(d) = n — the fundamental totient sum

conclusion.summary: Inclusion-exclusion applications fully verified: sieve formulas, totient for prime products, surjection count, derangement formula and recurrence, divisor-totient identity. 41 theorems, 382 lines, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The IE principle unifies seemingly disparate counting results. The derangement recurrence is a classic application with connections to the subfactorial and e. The divisor-totient identity is foundational for multiplicative number theory.
openQuestions: Formalize the general IE formula for k sets (not just 2 and 3)
Prove the derangement limit D(n)/n! → 1/e using the Taylor series for e^{-1}
Apply IE to prove the Möbius inversion formula
